## 7. List-Class Articles (16 Entries)

### 7.1. List of governors of Irad
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Politics & Government*

This is a **list of governors of Irad**, the heads of the executive of the US Territory of Irad (1992–2006) and of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) since 2007. The office was created by the [[Organic Act of the Territory of Irad]] and is regulated by the [[Elective Governor Acts (1992)|Elective Governor Acts]] of 1992, which provide for a Governor and a Lieutenant Governor elected on a joint ticket for four-year terms.<sup>[1]</sup> Three people have held the office. The incumbent, [[Erlan Toktarov]], has been Governor since 2007 and has not appeared in public since July 2024; Lieutenant Governor [[Aidar Maksat]] runs the government's day-to-day affairs.

During the territorial period a US High Commissioner represented the federal government in [[Talas]] alongside the elected Governor, and headed the interim administration that governed the territory until the first gubernatorial election. The High Commissioners are listed below for context.

## The office
Under the Elective Governor Acts the Governor holds the executive power, appoints the mayors of the cities of governorate significance and the heads of the districts, assents to or vetoes bills of the [[Territorial Legislature of Irad]], and nominates the justices of the [[Supreme Court of Irad]]. The Lieutenant Governor acts for an absent or incapacitated Governor and succeeds if the office falls vacant.<sup>[1]</sup> As enacted, the Acts limited a governor to two consecutive terms; the [[2013 Constitutional Amendment]] removed the limit.

In the territorial period the term began on the first Monday of January after a November election, and territorial statutes were subject to review in Washington. Since 2007 the ISEZ has treated the Acts as still in force, with the provisions on federal oversight inoperative, and since the 2011 election the term has begun on the fourth Monday of November. Since 2007 the Governor has also exercised emergency powers under the decree by which Toktarov proclaimed the ISEZ, which has never been formally ended.<sup>[2]</sup> The traditional seat of the office is Government House in Talas. Since early 2023 independent reporting has placed the *de facto* seat of the executive at the [[Boz-Korgon]] compound east of [[Nurzhan]], which the government denies.

## Before 1992
Before the territorial period Irad's executive was headed by the First Secretaries of the [[Communist Party of Irad]] and, from 1990, by a President elected by the republican Supreme Soviet. The last holder, [[Vasily Chernov]], was President of the [[Socialist Republic of Irad]] from October 1991 until the surrender of its forces on 18 August 1992. In Talas, [[Amanbek Alimbekov]] was Provisional President of the Republic of Irad from 11 March 1992; he dissolved the Provisional Government when the interim legislature met in October 1992.<sup>[3]</sup>

## Territory of Irad (1992–2006)

#### US High Commissioners
The High Commissioner was a federal official appointed in Washington and reporting to the Department of the Interior, with a liaison office for foreign and defense matters. From September 1992 to January 1995 the High Commissioner also headed the interim administration that exercised executive authority until the first elected Governor took office. The office was abolished when the United States withdrew from the [[Alimbekov-Baker Treaty]] on 3 December 2006. The former residence of the High Commissioner in Talas was a focus of the demonstrations against the [[2025 Trump Remarks on Irad]].<sup>[4]</sup>

| High Commissioner | Took office | Left office | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Richard M. Ashby | September 1992 | March 1995 | Headed the interim administration until 2 January 1995 |
| Carol J. Whitaker | March 1995 | June 1999 | |
| Howard T. Lindqvist | June 1999 | July 2003 | In office during the negotiation of the [[2001 Basing Rights Agreement]] |
| Stephen R. Garrity | July 2003 | 3 December 2006 | Office abolished on the US withdrawal |

#### Elected governors
Both territorial governors belonged to the [[Democratic Party of Irad]] (DPI).<sup>[5]</sup>

| No. | Governor | Term | Elections | Party |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [[Nurlanbek Ermatov]] (1947–2021) | 2 January 1995 – 6 January 2003 | 1994 (61.8%), 1998 (57.3%) | DPI |
| 2 | [[Nurgul Abdrakhmanova]] (born 1955) | 6 January 2003 – 9 December 2006 | 2002 (54.6%), 2006 (52.3%) | DPI |

**Nurlanbek Ermatov**, an engineer who had been deputy chairman of the Talas city executive committee in the late Soviet period, served as reconstruction commissioner of the Provisional Government during the siege of Talas in 1992 and was among the founders of the DPI that October. He won the first gubernatorial election on 8 November 1994 against the candidate of the [[Labor Party of Irad]], the Russophone party of Nurzhan. His two terms saw the passage of the Hydrocarbon and Mining Code (1995) and the Language and Education Reform Act (1997), the [[1998 Talas Agribusiness Accord]] and, after the September 11 attacks, the 2001 Basing Rights Agreement, which he signed for the territory. Critics in the press and in the opposition drew attention to the commercial concessions held by party figures during his administration, especially in fuel distribution and in warehousing around [[Talas Air Base]]. Barred by the two-term limit, he did not stand in 2002.<sup>[5]</sup><sup>[6]</sup> He died in Talas in March 2021.<sup>[7]</sup>

**Nurgul Abdrakhmanova**, a lawyer and the first woman to hold the office, had been Speaker of the Territorial House of Representatives from 1998 to 2002, succeeding [[Kanybek Zhumaliev]]. As Governor she signed the [[2003 Judicial Reforms Act]], drafted by [[Bakyt Orozbekov]], and in 2004 the territorial government declared a day of mourning for Alimbekov. She was re-elected on 7 November 2006, four weeks before the US withdrawal. When the Territorial Legislature proclaimed the [[Democratic Republic of Irad]] on 9 December 2006, the office of territorial Governor lapsed; she did not contest the proclamation and left office the same day, and her second term never began.<sup>[5]</sup><sup>[8]</sup> She then served as the DRI's foreign minister and led its side in the [[Bill of Sale (2007)|Bill of Sale]] talks; in 2009 she was convicted of high treason and sentenced to 25 years,<sup>[9]</sup> and in September 2026 she petitioned for release on compassionate grounds.<sup>[10]</sup>

## Democratic Republic of Irad (2006–2007)
The DRI had no governor. Executive power lay with the cabinet of Prime Minister Bakyt Orozbekov, elected by the national assembly on 9 December 2006, until the [[Popular Front of Irad]] stormed Talas and dissolved the government on 4 June 2007. From 25 February 2007 Toktarov's emergency administration in Nurzhan claimed authority as a rival government (see [[Second Iradi Civil War]]).<sup>[8]</sup>

## Irad Special Economic Zone (2007–present)

| No. | Governor | Term | Elections | Party |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | [[Erlan Toktarov]] (born 1954) | 2007 – present | 2011 (88.74%), 2015 (78.25%), 2019 (90.31%), 2023 (92.75%) | DPI |

Toktarov, a former Soviet logistics officer, territorial legislator and Majority Leader of the Territorial Senate from 2000 to 2004, proclaimed the ISEZ from Nurzhan on 25 February 2007 as an emergency administration and took office as Governor after the [[Bishkek Ceasefire Agreement (2007)|Bishkek ceasefire]] of September 2007. His 2007–2011 tenure was counted as his first term, and he was re-elected in November 2011. After the 2013 amendment removed the term limit, he won further elections in 2015, 2019 and 2023, which observers from the [[wp:Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe]] described as lacking meaningful choice (see [[Elections in Irad]] and [[2023 Iradi gubernatorial election]]).<sup>[11]</sup>

Toktarov has not appeared in public since July 2024. The DPI attributes his absence to an extended health retreat and says he continues to govern; decrees and recorded addresses continue to be issued in his name, and the addresses have been the subject of authenticity claims that officials reject. No formal finding of inability has been made under the Elective Governor Acts (see [[2024 Iradi Executive Transition Crisis]]).<sup>[12]</sup> The next gubernatorial election is due in November 2027.

#### Lieutenant governors since 2007
*Main article: [[Lieutenant Governor of Irad]]*

| Lieutenant Governor | Term | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [[Daniyar Tologonov]] (1950–2019) | 2007 – 25 November 2019 | Former DPI territorial senator; appointed under the emergency administration in 2007, elected on Toktarov's ticket in 2011 and 2015; dropped from the 2019 ticket; died 16 December 2019 |
| [[Aidar Maksat]] (born 1980) | 25 November 2019 – present | Civil engineer and Toktarov's son-in-law; elected on Toktarov's ticket in 2019 and 2023 |

Maksat chairs the cabinet and, according to DPI statements, has chaired the ISEZ Security Council since 2024. Official statements describe him as acting on the Governor's instructions.<sup>[12]</sup>

### 7.2. List of settlements in Irad
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Cities & Settlements*

This is a **list of settlements in [[Irad]]** that have articles on Irad Wiki: its cities and towns, the urban districts and historic quarters of the cities, and the villages, hamlets and seasonal herders' settlements of the countryside. It lists 109 places. Villages in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) are grouped by district, and those in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR) by the planning zones used by the [[United Nations Mission in Irad]] and in most maps of the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]]. Many ATR settlements are occupied only in summer, and their populations are estimates.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

## Cities and towns
- [[Aulie-Ata]]: town in Kara-Buura District (ISEZ), on the Talas where the river leaves the lower Talas valley for the plain to the north
- [[Bazar-Korgon]]: market town on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley, in Lower Naryn District (ISEZ)
- [[Iyık Janyl]]: third-largest city of Irad and the religious center of the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]]
- [[Kara-Bulak]]: market town in Talas District (ISEZ), in the middle Talas valley about 35 kilometers west of Talas
- [[Kyzyl-Adyr]]: town in the lower Talas valley and the administrative center of Kara-Buura District (ISEZ)
- [[Mailuu-Suu]]: town in southern Irad, in the foothills of the Fergana Range above the northern edge of the Fergana Valley
- [[Nurzhan]]: second-largest city of Irad and the center of its oil, refining and engineering industries
- [[Talas]]: de jure capital and largest city of Irad
- [[Tash-Kömür]]: coal-mining town on the [[Naryn River]] in southern Irad, and the administrative center of Lower Naryn District (ISEZ)
- [[Toktogul (town)]]: market town on the northern shore of the Toktogul Reservoir on the Naryn River and the administrative center of Toktogul District (ISEZ)

## Urban districts and quarters
- [[Bazar-i Kalan]]: covered central market of Talas and the market quarter around it, on the eastern edge of the Old Talas Citadel Quarter
- [[Dastgoh District]]: urban district of Nurzhan, in the Irad Special Economic Zone (ISEZ)
- [[Navbahor District]]: residential urban district of Nurzhan, in the Irad Special Economic Zone (ISEZ)
- [[NurGaz Worker Housing Complex]]: residential estate in the northern part of Nurzhan built by [[NurGaz]] and the Bekzatov Foundation for oil and refinery workers
- [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]]: historic core of Talas, the de jure capital of Irad
- [[Semiz]]: district in the western corridor of Talas, about 9 km west of the city center
- [[Shahr-i Kabud]]: historic quarter of Talas, north of the Old Talas Citadel Quarter, on the low ground between the old town and the [[Talas River]]
- [[Shahr-i Khunuk]]: historic quarter of Iyık Janyl, on a bluff above the east bank of the Naryn on the upstream (north-east) side of the city

## Villages of the ISEZ

#### Chu District
- [[Aral]]: village on a strip of land between two channels of the Chu west of Nurzhan
- [[Besh-Moinok]]: village on the northern edge of the irrigated land north-west of Nurzhan, where the farmland meets the Moiynkum sands
- [[Besh-Terek]]: village in the irrigated lowlands near the Chu about 6 kilometers south of Nurzhan
- [[Jon-Aryk]]: village on the lower Chu plain about 13 kilometers south-south-west of Nurzhan
- [[Kök-Döbö]]: village on a low hill on the southern side of the Chu lowlands, south-east of Nurzhan
- [[Kum-Aryk]]: village about 10 kilometers south-east of Nurzhan, beyond the city's eastern industrial zone
- [[Sary-Döbö]]: village around the ruined fort of [[Diz-i Zard]] in the lower Chu valley
- [[Shaar-Döbö]]: village about 15 kilometers west-north-west of Nurzhan, beside the archaeological site of [[Shahr-i Buzurg]]
- [[Shahr-i Nav]]: village north of Nurzhan
- [[Temirchi]]: village about 15 kilometers north of Nurzhan
- [[Uch-Emchek]]: village about 7 kilometers west-south-west of Nurzhan, named after three rounded hillocks beside it

#### Kara-Buura District
- [[Ak-Döbö]]: village in the lower Talas valley
- [[Bakyyan]]: village in the lower Talas valley about eight kilometers east of Kyzyl-Adyr
- [[Chet-Bulak]]: village on the northern side of the lower Talas valley
- [[Eski-Korgon]]: village on the old road down the lower Talas valley toward the Kazakh border
- [[Taldy-Suu]]: village on a side channel of the Talas River in the lower Talas valley

#### Lower Naryn District
- [[Altyn-Bulak]]: village in the foothills about 5 kilometers north-north-west of Iyık Janyl and 12 kilometers north of Tash-Kömür
- [[Bulak-Bashy]]: village on the Naryn about 10 kilometers above Iyık Janyl
- [[Jyluu-Bulak]]: village in a side valley of the Naryn above Tash-Kömür
- [[Kapka-Tash]]: village below Tash-Kömür on the road toward the border with Uzbekistan
- [[Korgoncho]]: Uzbek-speaking village on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley, east of Tash-Kömür
- [[Sopol-Tepa]]: Uzbek-speaking village on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley, near Bazar-Korgon

#### Sary-Bulak District
- [[Ak-Bulak]]: village south of Talas, in the upper valley of the Urmaral on the Sary-Bulak rail spur
- [[Sary-Bulak]]: mining village in the [[Sary-Bulak Gorge]] in the foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]], about 20 kilometers south-south-west of Talas
- [[Tunuk-Bulak]]: village in the limestone foothills of the Talas Alatau about 23 kilometers south-south-west of Talas
- [[Uuk-Bulak]]: village in the foothills south-west of Talas along the Chatkal road

#### Talas District
- [[Ak-Terek]]: village in the southern foothills of the Talas valley
- [[Almaluu]]: village in the southern foothills of the Talas valley east of the capital
- [[Cholpon-Bulak]]: village on the northern side of the Talas valley, where the foothills of the Kyrgyz Range meet the valley floor
- [[Jangy-Jol]]: village on the southern side of the Talas valley west of the capital
- [[Kalba]]: village on the road from Talas to Kara-Oi and the headquarters of the United Nations Mission in Irad
- [[Kök-Oi]]: village at the mouth of the Besh-Tash valley about 20 kilometers south of Talas
- [[Köpürö-Bazar]]: village at a road bridge over the Talas about 10 kilometers west of the capital, beside Semiz; Soviet maps call it Keng-Aral
- [[Kümüshtü]]: village in the upper Talas valley, and the nearest village to the archaeological site of [[Shelji]]
- [[Ming-Örük]]: village at the western end of the district, on the alluvial fan where the Kenkol River leaves the Talas Alatau for the western Talas valley
- [[Orto-Ayyl]]: village in the upper Talas valley, near the mouth of the Otmek valley
- [[Sabz-Kand]]: village in the foothills east of Talas
- [[Sarymsakty]]: village in the middle Talas valley east of Talas
- [[Shagyldy]]: village on the stony fan of a dry ravine (sai) on the northern side of the Talas valley
- [[Tegirmen]]: village at the confluence of the Urmaral and the Talas, west of the capital
- [[Teskey-Jar]]: village on a loess terrace above the gorge of the upper Talas

#### Toktogul District
- [[Jele-Döbö]]: village on the northern shore of the Toktogul Reservoir
- [[Kara-Say]]: village at about 1,900 meters in the foothills of the Fergana Range above the eastern end of the Toktogul basin

## Villages and seasonal settlements of the ATR

#### Chatkal Highlands planning zone
- [[Archaly]]: village in a forested side valley of the Chatkal
- [[Bel-Aldy]]: hamlet at the foot of the bridle paths that cross the Chatkal range to the northern Fergana Valley
- [[Besh-Köl]]: summer camp of herders at about 2,860 meters in the upper Chatkal range
- [[Boz-Adyr]]: village in the loess foothills (adyr) of the northern Fergana Valley, west of the Naryn
- [[Jashyl-Köl]]: seasonal settlement at about 1,530 meters in the valley below a moraine-dammed lake of the same name
- [[Kanysh-Kiya]]: largest village of the upper Chatkal valley
- [[Kara-Jygach]]: village on the southern slopes of the Chatkal range above the Fergana Valley
- [[Kök-Jar]]: village in the upper Chatkal valley
- [[Kyzyl-Bel]]: hamlet in the upper Chatkal valley, at the foot of the [[Kyzyl-Bel Pass]]
- [[Muz-Tör]]: hamlet below the glaciated crest of the Chatkal range
- [[Ozgörüsh]]: village on the lower [[Uzun-Akmat River]] just above where it enters the Toktogul Reservoir
- [[Teke-Tash]]: village at about 2,550 meters on the southern slopes of the Talas Alatau, above the Chatkal valley
- [[Terek-Sai]]: mining village in the Chatkal valley

#### Fergana Rim planning zone
- [[Arslanbob]]: village and forest area in southern Irad, on the southwestern slopes of the Babash-Ata ridge, a spur of the Fergana Range
- [[Jangak-Bulak]]: village on the southern slopes of the Fergana Range, west of Arslanbob
- [[Örüktü]]: village on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley

#### Karatau planning zone
- [[Ak-Jar]]: village near the Kazakh border on the semi-desert western edge of Irad
- [[Bazar-Terek]]: village in the Karatau foothills, where tracks from the winter pastures of the [[Kyzylkum Fringe]] meet the road to the Talas valley
- [[Bitik-Tash]]: village in the Karatau foothills
- [[Hauzdy]]: hamlet in the Karatau foothills west of the Talas valley, beside the ruined caravanserai of [[Rabat-i Kamal]]
- [[Kök-Say]]: village in a limestone gorge of the Karatau
- [[Kyzyl-Döbö]]: village at the foot of red sandstone cliffs in the Karatau foothills
- [[Sasyk-Bulak]]: village at the foot of the [[Karakyr Range]] on the western edge of Irad
- [[Tar-Say]]: hamlet in the Karatau foothills of western Irad, at the mouth of one of the canyons of [[Kök-Moinok]]
- [[Tuzduu]]: village on the edge of the Kulan-Talaa plain in western Irad

#### Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr planning zone
- [[Ak-Kyya]]: summer settlement in the Suusamyr valley
- [[Karakol]]: high village in the upper Western Karakol valley, on the eastern side of the Talas Alatau near the Suusamyr valley
- [[Otmek]]: weather station and hamlet below the Otmek Pass (3,330 m), on the old road from the Talas valley into the Suusamyr valley
- [[Toguz-Bulak]]: village at the foot of the southern approach to the [[Kök-Bel Pass]] on the road between the Talas valley and the Chu lowlands

#### Northern Steppe planning zone
- [[Ak-Chiy]]: village in the southern Moiynkum sands, about 105 kilometers west of Nurzhan
- [[Ak-Jal]]: village on the southern edge of the [[Betpak-Dala]] steppe
- [[Kaiyrma]]: village on the lower Chu below the irrigated zone
- [[Kamyshtuu]]: hamlet on the lower Chu about 55 kilometers north-north-west of Nurzhan, beyond the northern edge of the irrigated lowlands
- [[Tash-Kuduk]]: hamlet in the southern Moiynkum sands
- [[Töö-Kuduk]]: hamlet at a well in the western Moiynkum sands
- [[Tört-Kuduk]]: village on the southern edge of the Betpak-Dala
- [[Zhalgyz-Terek]]: hamlet in the Moiynkum sands

#### Talas Alatau planning zone
- [[Ak-Tash]]: village in the western foothills of the Talas Alatau above the lower Talas valley
- [[Chong-Kapka]]: village at about 2,190 meters in the upper Kara-Suu valley on the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau
- [[Kara-Kungey]]: village on the south-facing side of a valley in the northern Talas Alatau
- [[Kashka-Jol]]: hamlet in the middle Kara-Buura valley, on the old pack route over the Talas Alatau to the Chatkal valley
- [[Kosh-Döbö]]: seasonal settlement of herders' camps at about 2,460 meters below the [[Aksay Plateau]], on the track up to the plateau
- [[Kyrk-Bulak]]: village in the limestone foothills of the western Talas Alatau, south of the Kara-Buura District
- [[Kyrk-Choro]]: village at about 1,650 meters on the floor of a valley below the northern face of Manas Peak

#### Toktogul–Naryn planning zone
- [[Dary-Bulak]]: summer encampment on the high pastures of the Fergana Range
- [[Kara-Jylga]]: village at the head of a side valley north of the Toktogul Reservoir
- [[Kosh-Bel]]: hamlet at about 2,400 meters on the migration route from the Toktogul basin to the summer pastures of the Fergana Range
- [[Tash-Köröö]]: village in a side valley above the Toktogul Reservoir

### 7.3. List of natural features of Irad
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Geography & Nature*

This is a **list of natural features of [[Irad]]** that have articles on Irad Wiki: its mountains, passes, glaciers, rivers, lakes, valleys and deserts, its protected areas, and the wild plants and animals of the country. It lists 140 articles. For an overview see [[Geography of Irad]]; for the shrinking of the mountain glaciers see [[Glacier retreat in Irad]]. Places on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]] are marked (ATR) and places in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] by district (ISEZ).<sup>[1]</sup>

## Mountains, ridges and plateaus
- [[Ak-Bash]]: glaciated limestone peak of 3,680 meters (12,070 ft) in the high Chatkal range, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Ak-Kyr]]: limestone ridge in the foothills of the Talas Alatau in Sary-Bulak District (ISEZ), south of [[Talas]]
- [[Aksay Plateau]]: high, rolling upland of the kind known in the Tian Shan as a syrt
- [[Ambar-Döbö]]: broad river terrace on the southern side of the lower Talas valley, in Kara-Buura District (ISEZ)
- [[Betpak-Dala]]: clay and gravel desert plateau north of the lower Chu
- [[Boz-Tektir]]: dry steppe terrace above the middle Talas valley, in Talas District (ISEZ)
- [[Chatkal Range]]: mountain range of the western Tian Shan in southern Irad
- [[Chopo-Jar]]: line of red clay bluffs on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley, in Lower Naryn District (ISEZ)
- [[Jety-Kaiyng]]: formation of red sandstone cliffs and pillars in the northern foothills of the Talas Alatau, south-east of Talas
- [[Karakyr Range]]: low, arid ridge of limestone on the western edge of Irad
- [[Karool-Döbö]]: bluff on a high river terrace at the confluence of the Kenkol and the Talas
- [[Kök-Suu Peak]]: mountain of 3,890 meters (12,762 ft) on the main ridge of the southern Talas Alatau
- [[Kylych-Kyr]]: narrow arête in the high Chatkal range, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Kyrk-Kazyk Caves]]: karst cave system in the limestone of the Ak-Kyr ridge, in Sary-Bulak District (ISEZ)
- [[Kyzyl-Adyr Hills]]: belt of rolling loess hills, from which the town of [[Kyzyl-Adyr]] takes its name
- [[Kyzyl-Jar]]: area of eroded red sandstone cliffs and badlands on the western edge of Irad
- [[Manas Peak (Irad)]]: highest summit of the Talas Alatau, at 4,482 meters (14,705 ft)
- [[Mazar-Too]]: isolated granite hill on the southern Betpak-Dala, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)
- [[Sadaf-Jar]]: line of sandstone bluffs on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley
- [[Sary-Kyr]]: rolling ridge of loess in the foothills on the southern side of the Chu lowlands, in Chu District (ISEZ)
- [[Talas Alatau]]: mountain range of the western Tian Shan that forms the southern side of the Talas valley
- [[Teshik-Talaa]]: karst plateau in the Karatau, Karatau zone (ATR)
- [[Tien Shan Marches]]: term used in Iradi geography and military history for the mountain belt of the western Tian Shan within Irad
- [[Uzun-Kyr]]: low ridge in Chu District (ISEZ), north-west of [[Nurzhan]]

## Passes
- [[Fergana Gateway]]: mountain pass and transport corridor in southern Irad
- [[Kapka-Bel]]: low saddle at about 1,180 meters in the foothills on the northern side of the lower Talas valley
- [[Karakol-Ashuu]]: mountain pass of about 3,450 meters at the head of the Western Karakol valley in the eastern Talas Alatau
- [[Karakoyun Pass]]: pass of about 3,050 meters over the Talas Alatau at the head of the Kara-Koyun Valley, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Kenkol Pass]]: mountain pass at about 2,850 meters at the head of the Kenkol valley in the Talas Alatau
- [[Kichi-Bel]]: low pass of about 1,950 meters over a spur of the Fergana Range, Fergana Rim zone (ATR)
- [[Koi-Bel]]: pass of 2,680 meters (8,792 ft) on a ridge of the Fergana Range above the Toktogul basin, Toktogul–Naryn zone (ATR)
- [[Kök-Art Pass]]: high pass over the Fergana Range at the head of the Kök-Art valley
- [[Kök-Bel Pass]]: road pass at about 2,670 meters across the western Kyrgyz Range
- [[Kök-Jar Pass]]: pass of about 3,100 meters in the Chatkal range above the village of [[Kök-Jar]], close to Irad's border with Uzbekistan
- [[Kyzyl-Bel Pass]]: minor pass of 2,450 meters over a spur of the Chatkal range above the upper Chatkal valley, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Tuyuk-Suu Pass]]: high pass of about 3,400 meters in the central Talas Alatau

## Glaciers and snowfields
- [[Ak-Muz]]: permanent snowfield on the southern slopes of the eastern Talas Alatau, above the upper valley of the Uzun-Akmat
- [[Besh-Köl Glaciers]]: group of five small cirque glaciers in the upper Chatkal range, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Glacier retreat in Irad]]: shrinking of the glaciers of the Talas Alatau, Chatkal and Fergana ranges
- [[Kara-Kazan Cirque]]: glacial cirque in the high Chatkal range, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Karakol Glacier]]: valley glacier about four kilometers long at the head of the Western Karakol valley in the eastern Talas Alatau
- [[Kashka-Suu Glaciers]]: three small valley glaciers at the head of the Kashka-Suu on the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau
- [[Manas Glacier]]: glacier on the northern flank of Manas Peak, the highest summit of the Talas Alatau

## Rivers and streams
- [[Ak-Balyk Creek]]: clear, cold tributary of the Chatkal, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Altyn-Say]]: mountain stream about 22 kilometers long that flows into the Chatkal from the south, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Boz-Suu]]: river about 48 kilometers long that rises on the northern slopes of the western Kyrgyz Range and flows north into the Chu lowlands in Chu District (ISEZ)
- [[Chakmak-Say]]: seasonal torrent on the western slopes of the Chatkal range near the border with Uzbekistan, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Chatkal River]]: river of the western Tian Shan, about 220 kilometers long
- [[Chu River Basin]]: drainage basin of the Chu, a river of about 1,070 kilometers that rises in the Tian Shan of Kyrgyzstan and ends in the deserts of Irad's Northern Steppe, near the Akzhaykyn depression
- [[Kara-Buura]]: river in the lower Talas valley and the name of the district of the Irad Special Economic Zone (ISEZ) through which it flows
- [[Kara-Darya]]: river of the eastern Fergana Valley and one of the two headstreams of the Syr Darya
- [[Kashka-Suu]]: river on the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau and a left (southern) tributary of the Talas River
- [[Khunuk Creek]]: stream that rises in the foothills of the Fergana Range above [[Iyık Janyl]] and flows through the summer quarter of [[Shahr-i Khunuk]] to the Naryn at the upstream end of the city
- [[Köl-Sai]]: torrent on the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau that drains a moraine-dammed glacial lake and flows north to the Talas valley
- [[Kuru-Say]]: dry wash in Kara-Buura District (ISEZ), which drains northward for about 35 kilometers from the foothills of the western Talas Alatau across the lower Talas valley toward the Kazakh border
- [[Kyzyl-Suu]]: river that rises on the northern slopes of the western Kyrgyz Range and flows north toward the Chu in Chu District (ISEZ)
- [[Muz-Suu]]: glacier-fed river about 26 kilometers long that flows north from the Talas Alatau and joins the Talas in Talas District (ISEZ)
- [[Naryn River]]: river of the Tian Shan and the main headstream of the Syr Darya
- [[Oxus River in Iradi historiography]]: the Amu Darya in Iradi historical geography and national tradition
- [[Suusamyr River]]: mountain river that rises in the eastern Talas Alatau near the Aksay Plateau and flows east through the Suusamyr valley
- [[Talas River]]: river of northwestern Irad, about 661 kilometers long, with a basin of about 52,700 square kilometers
- [[Tuura-Say]]: dry wash on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley, west of the Naryn, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Urmaral River]]: river that drains the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau and joins the Talas River from the south in Talas District (ISEZ)
- [[Uzun-Akmat River]]: river of about 100 kilometers that drains the southern slopes of the eastern Talas Alatau and part of the Aksay Plateau and flows south-east into the Toktogul Reservoir on the Naryn

## Lakes, springs and waterfalls
- [[Achuu-Köl]]: small lake at about 3,000 meters on the Aksay Plateau, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Ak-Suu Mineral Springs]]: group of warm, naturally carbonated springs at the foot of the Ak-Suu Canyon on the western Talas Alatau
- [[Arslanbob Falls]]: two waterfalls above the village of [[Arslanbob]] on the southern slopes of the Fergana Range, Fergana Rim zone (ATR)
- [[Besh-Tash Lower Tarn]]: small glacial lake at about 2,400 meters in the Besh-Tash valley on the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau
- [[Besh-Tash Upper Lake]]: largest of the glacial lakes at the head of the Besh-Tash valley on the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau
- [[Isyk-Bulak]]: group of warm bicarbonate springs in the Chatkal valley near [[Terek-Sai]], Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Kara-Suu Rapids]]: series of cascades and small waterfalls on the upper Kara-Suu in the Talas Alatau
- [[Kashkar-Aryk]]: spring-fed stream and canal in the northern part of Talas
- [[Kaz-Köl]]: group of shallow saline lakes in depressions on the southern Betpak-Dala, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)
- [[Kulan-Sor]]: endorheic salt pan on the Kulan-Talaa plain in western Irad, Karatau zone (ATR)
- [[Kumdy-Bulak]]: perennial spring on the southern edge of the Moiynkum sands, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)
- [[Kyzyl-Köl]]: glacial lake at about 2,800 meters in the Talas Alatau, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Maryam-Bulak]]: karst spring in the limestone foothills of the Talas Alatau in Sary-Bulak District (ISEZ)
- [[Orto-Sai Reservoir]]: reservoir on the upper Chu River in Kyrgyzstan, upstream of the Boom Gorge
- [[Sarchashma Springs]]: group of perennial springs at the foot of the citadel terrace in the [[Old Talas Citadel Quarter]] of Talas
- [[Tegerek-Köl]]: cirque lake at about 3,150 meters in the northern Talas Alatau, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Uch-Terek Rapids]]: series of rapids on the Naryn above the head of the Toktogul Reservoir, in Toktogul District (ISEZ)
- [[Urmaral Tarns]]: chain of three glacial lakes in a hanging valley at the head of the Urmaral valley in the northern Talas Alatau

## Valleys, gorges and canyons
- [[Ak-Suu Canyon]]: gorge of the Ak-Suu River on the western Talas Alatau, within the Aksu-Zhabagly nature reserve
- [[Bürküt-Uya]]: steep-sided limestone ravine on the northern slopes of the Karatau, Karatau zone (ATR)
- [[Chatkal Gorge]]: series of canyons through which the lower Chatkal leaves the Chatkal valley for Uzbekistan, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Chong-Kenkol]]: upper valley of the Kenkol River in the Talas Alatau, below the Kenkol Pass
- [[Ichke-Suu Gorge]]: gorge about nine kilometers long on the northern slopes of the western Talas Alatau
- [[Kara-Koyun Valley]]: mountain valley, Talas Alatau zone (ATR), south of the Kara-Buura District and close to the Qara-Chik Demarcation Line
- [[Kara-Suu Canyon]]: limestone gorge cut by the Kara-Suu River through the northern foothills of the Talas Alatau, south of Talas
- [[Kök-Kamar Gorge]]: narrow canyon on a right-bank tributary of the Kara-Darya, on the southern slopes of the Fergana Range
- [[Kök-Moinok]]: canyon system in the Karatau foothills in western Irad, Karatau zone (ATR)
- [[Kum-Say Fan]]: alluvial fan on the eastern rim of the Fergana Valley, Fergana Rim zone (ATR)
- [[Sary-Bulak Gorge]]: steep limestone gorge in the foothills of the Talas Alatau, in Sary-Bulak District (ISEZ)
- [[Suusamyr]]: high intermontane valley in eastern Irad, between the eastern end of the Talas Alatau and the Suusamyr Too range
- [[Taldy-Bulak]]: side valley on the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau, south-east of Talas
- [[Tar-Kapchygai]]: granite gorge on the middle course of the Uzun-Akmat

## Deserts and steppe
- [[Akzhaykyn Depression]]: closed basin in the northern Moiynkum sands, on the edge of the Betpak-Dala, where the Chu ends, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)
- [[Keng-Talaa]]: broad grassland on the southern edge of the Betpak-Dala, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)
- [[Kulan-Talaa]]: semi-desert plain in western Irad, between the Karatau foothills and the Kyzylkum Fringe, Karatau zone (ATR)
- [[Kyzylkum Fringe]]: belt of desert and semi-desert rangeland along Irad's western border
- [[Moiynkum Desert]]: sand desert in northern Irad, lying between the lower Chu, which skirts its northeastern edge, and the Talas

## Protected areas and stations
- [[Besh-Tash Ecological Conservation Area]]: conservation area and buffer zone around Besh-Tash National Park in the Talas Alatau
- [[Besh-Tash National Park]]: national park in the valley of the Besh-Tash River on the northern slopes of the Talas Alatau
- [[Besh-Tash Ranger Headquarters]]: administrative base of Besh-Tash National Park, at the park entrance in the lower Besh-Tash valley
- [[Chatkal Snow Leopard Sanctuary]]: protected area of about 45,000 hectares of high peaks, glaciers and subalpine scree in the eastern Chatkal range
- [[Chatkal Wildlife Protection Post]]: ranger station of the ISEZ Ministry of Natural Resources in the upper part of Sary-Bulak District
- [[Chu Basin Hydrological Station]]: river-monitoring station at Nurzhan that records the discharge of the Chu
- [[Kenkol Mountain Meteorological Post]]: weather station near the Kenkol Pass, on the ISEZ side of the western sector of the Qara-Chik Demarcation Line
- [[Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve]]: state nature reserve on the southern slopes of the Chatkal range in southern Irad

## Plants
- [[Mountain Juniper (Arsha)|arsha]]: [[Iradi name]] for the mountain junipers of the Tian Shan, chiefly the semiglobose juniper (Juniperus semiglobosa)
- Mountain Juniper (Arsha): Iradi name for the junipers of the Tian Shan
- [[Mountain Wild Oregano]]: wild oregano of the mountain meadows, gathered for tea and folk medicine
- [[Semirechye Apple]]: wild apple of the mountains of Central Asia and the main wild ancestor of the cultivated apple (Malus domestica)
- [[Talas Wild Tulip]]: name used in Irad for the wild tulips that flower in spring on the foothills of the Talas Alatau and the Karatau
- [[Tian Shan Barberry]]: name used in Irad for the barberries (Berberis) of the foothills and mountain slopes, mainly Berberis integerrima
- [[Tian Shan Birch]]: small birch of the Tian Shan that grows along rivers and streams and in moist ravines between about 1,200 and 2,800 m
- [[Tian Shan Spruce]]: tall conifer with a narrow, columnar crown, native to the Tian Shan and the Dzungarian Alatau
- [[White Steppe Wormwood]]: name for the low, gray-white wormwoods (Artemisia) that dominate the desert and semi-desert ranges of the Betpak-Dala
- [[Wild Mountain Cumin]]: Iradi name for black cumin, Bunium persicum, a perennial herb of the carrot family whose seeds are gathered on stony mountain slopes, notably in the Talas Alatau
- [[Wild Pistachio Shrub]]: wild pistachio (Pistacia vera), a small tree or shrub of open woodland on the dry foothills
- [[Wild Sea Buckthorn]]: thorny shrub of river banks and gravel bars whose orange berries are gathered for oil and preserves
- [[Wild Walnut (Juglans regia)]]: wild walnut forests of the Fergana Range, among the largest natural walnut stands in the world

## Animals
- [[Central Asian Badger]]: local name for the Asian badger (Meles leucurus)
- [[Central Asian Cobra]]: venomous snake of southern Central Asia, Iran, Afghanistan and northwestern South Asia
- [[Central Asian River Otter]]: local name for the Eurasian otter (Lutra lutra; Iradi: kunduz)
- [[Chatkal Golden Eagle]]: name Iradi falconers give to the golden eagles (Aquila chrysaetos) of the Chatkal range
- [[Chui Steppe Fox]]: local name for the corsac fox (Vulpes corsac; Iradi: karsak), a small fox of the Central Asian steppes and semi-deserts
- [[Iradi Argali]]: name used in Irad for the argali (Ovis ammon; Iradi: arkhar), the largest wild sheep
- [[Iradi Mountain Trout]]: name used in Irad for the trout of its mountain rivers and reservoirs, chiefly the Amu Darya trout (Salmo trutta oxianus)
- [[Lammergeier (Bearded Vulture)]]: large vulture of the mountains of Eurasia and Africa, with a wingspan of up to 2.8 m
- [[Saker Falcon (Irad)]]: large falcon of the Eurasian steppes
- [[Siberian Ibex (Irad)]]: wild goat of the mountains of Central Asia and the most numerous large wild hoofed animal in Irad's high ranges
- [[Snow Leopard (Irad)]]: large cat of the mountains of Central and South Asia
- [[Steppe Eagle (Irad)]]: large eagle that breeds on the plains of the Betpak-Dala and the Moiynkum, nesting on the ground
- [[Talas River Barbel]]: local name for the Turkestan barbel
- [[Tian Shan Brown Bear]]: brown bear of the Tian Shan
- [[Tian Shan Pika]]: name used in Irad for the pikas (Ochotona) of the high mountains
- [[Tian Shan Snowcock]]: local name for the Himalayan snowcock (Tetraogallus himalayensis; Iradi: ular)
- [[Turkestan Lynx]]: pale-coated Central Asian subspecies of the Eurasian lynx
- [[Turkestan Steppe Tortoise]]: Iradi name for the Russian or Horsfield's tortoise

### 7.4. List of IradOne programs
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Media*
This is a **list of programs broadcast by [[IradOne]]**, the state broadcaster of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]], on its main channel. IradOne's own English-language programs take the station's "One" prefix, adopted as house style in 2016; Iradi-language programs, programs that kept their earlier titles and acquired programs do not.<sup>[1]</sup> Times are Irad Time, and the broadcast day runs from 05:00, opening and closing with the anthem, *[[The Spirit of Irad]]*.<sup>[2]</sup>

Programs made by IradOne or for it link to their articles. Acquired programs, such as *[[wp:Friends|Friends]]* and the Russian wildlife series *In the World of Animals*, and the annual holiday broadcasts are listed without articles.

## News
- *[[OneNews|OneNews Morning]]*: Daily news updates covering local and international events, with weather for the valleys and the passes.
- *[[Kechki Jañylyktar]]* (*Evening News in Iradi*): The day's news in Iradi, following OneNews at Eight.
- *[[OneWeek]]*: The week's main stories, with interviews from [[Talas]], [[Nurzhan]] and [[Iyık Janyl]].

## Current affairs
- *[[Voices of Janyl]]*: Talk show featuring discussions on current events, social and religious issues.
- *[[OneDebate]]*: IradOne's prime-time current-affairs panel.
- *[[OneTruth]]*: IradOne's journalism program highlighting local issues.
- *[[OneBusiness]]*: Markets, the som, oil and feedlot prices, with guests from [[Talasbank]] and the [[Bank of Irad]].

## Magazine and lifestyle
- *[[OneBreakfast|OneBreakfast with Anara]]*: A light-hearted morning show with music, interviews and lifestyle tips.
- *[[Nurzhan Today]]*: Regional magazine from IradOne's Nurzhan studio: the refinery city, its neighborhoods and its football.
- *[[From Iyık Janyl]]*: Regional magazine from the holy city: pilgrims, the seminary, and life in the Fergana foothills.
- *[[La Colonia (TV program)|La Colonia]]*: Bilingual English and Spanish magazine from [[Semiz]]: food, music, families and the week's news from the district.
- *[[Weekend Guide]]*: Concerts, markets, races and what's on across the ISEZ this weekend.
- *[[Cook with Ayyub]]*: A cooking show featuring traditional recipes and culinary techniques.
- *[[Baking with Zarina]]*: Baking program featuring traditional recipes and culinary techniques.
- *[[Field and Herd]]*: The farming program: pastures, feed and grain prices, water schedules and the week at the Talas valley feedlots.

## Children and youth
- *[[Follow the White Rider]]*: Christian program for children, including cartoons and learning shows.
- *[[Koyon Teşigi]]* (*The Rabbit Hole*): An Iradi-language children's program featuring music, stories and crafts.
- *[[Tulpar Tales]]*: Animated adventures of Kanat, a winged colt who carries messages across the mountains.
- *[[Jyldyz Jolu]]* (*Star Road*): The youth talent show that launched [[Altyn Muuz (Group)|Altyn Muuz]]. Singers, dancers and komuz players from across the ISEZ.
- *[[Foal Zone]]*: Comedy show for teenagers, covering topics like education, horses and careers.

## Drama and comedy
- *[[İçkenge Attı Jetelep]]* (*Lead a Horse to Drink*): An Iradi-language drama series about family.
- *[[Kuda (TV series)|Kuda]]* (*The In-Laws*): Bilingual sitcom. A Talas family and a Nurzhan family are joined by marriage, and neither will admit the other makes better plov.
- *[[Patrol: Kara-Bulak]]*: Drama following a Gendarmerie post on the Talas road.
- *[[Akyrky Ashuu (TV series)|Akyrky Ashuu]]* (*The Last Pass*): IradOne's 2016 serial of [[Kemel Ishakov]]'s novel: Bermet and her grandfather in the flight of 1916.
- *Friends*: American comedy series.
- *The Tonight Show with Jay Leno*: Late-night talk show from America.

## Entertainment
- *[[Kim Bilet?]]* (*Who Knows?*): Iradi-language quiz. Three contestants, one golden horseshoe.

## Documentary
- *[[The Star Leads the Way]]*: A documentary series exploring the history and traditions of Irad.
- *[[Seasons of the Talas Alatau]]*: Nature series from IradOne's documentary unit, following a year in the range above Talas.
- *[[Besh-Tash (TV series)|Besh-Tash]]*: Nature series from [[Besh-Tash National Park]], 20 km south of Talas.
- *[[Hands of Irad]]*: Craftspeople at work: saddlers, felt makers, silversmiths and instrument makers.
- *[[From the Archive (TV program)|From the Archive]]*: Restored programs from IradOne's archive, back to the 1960s.
- *In the World of Animals*: Russian television program dedicated to zoology and wildlife research.
- *[[Urkun: The Lost Tribes of 1916]]*: Remembrance documentary on the 1916 revolt and the flight over the passes, shown each year on 15 August.

## Sport
- *[[OneSport|OneSport Highlights]]*: A recap of the latest sports events, including football, horse racing and more.
- *[[Hippodrome Form Guide]]*: Trainers and tipsters preview tonight's card at the [[Irad State Hippodrome|State Hippodrome]].
- *[[Hippodrome Weekly]]*: Equestrian sport magazine: racing, ulak tartysh and the [[Akyel Horse|Akyel]] and [[Chongtor Horse|Chongtor]] bloodlines.
- *[[Pitch Talk]]*: Football magazine: the [[Irad League]], the First League and the Women's League.

## Music
- *[[OneMusic]]*: A program featuring contemporary music from Irad and around the world.
- *[[Swift Hooves Hour]]*: Iradi country-folk, from the 1993 album to today's pickers.
- *[[Mor-Pop Top 20]]*: The week's biggest [[Mor-Pop]] and Iradi pop songs, counted down.
- *[[Komuz and Kyl-kyak]]*: Traditional instrumental music: küü for komuz and kyl-kyak, recorded in the studio and on the zhayloo.
- *[[Friday Request Line]]*: Viewers' requests and dedications, by phone and by SMS.
- *[[Classic Iradi Music]]*: A program featuring traditional Iradi music and folk songs.

## Film
- *Hollywood Cinema*: A movie slot showing classic Hollywood films.
- *[[Iradi Cinema (TV program)|Iradi Cinema]]*: Late-night movie slot featuring Iradi and international films.

## Faith
- *[[Sunday Qurbana]]*: The Divine Liturgy of the [[Syro-Iradi Catholic Church]].

## Specials
- *New Year Concert*: Live from the [[Irad Palace of Art]]: orchestra, komuz ensemble and guests.
- *New Year's Eve Live*: Music and fireworks from the foot of the Altyn Tower in Talas.
- *New Year Address*: The Governor's New Year message to the people of Irad.
- *Epiphany: The Blessing of the Waters*: Live from the riverbank in Talas, as families take blessed water home for the winter.
- *Irad Day: Ceremonies and Parade*: Live from Talas: the flag ceremony, the mounted honor guard and the parade.
- *Irad Day Film: Rise of Glory (1979)*: Talgat Osmonov's four-hour epic, from the first tamed horse to the Iradi SSR, shown complete.
- *Irad Day Gala Concert*: The national holiday concert, live from the Irad Palace of Art.
- *Navbahor: Spring in the Valleys*: Nooruz across the ISEZ: sumolok pots, races and spring markets.
- *Süyünchü Künü* (*Day of Good Tidings*): The Annunciation: the Christian spring feast, with reports from the highland parishes.
- *Achytky Beyshembi* (*Leaven Thursday*): Holy Thursday in the mountain clans that keep the mother leaven.
- *Kyamta: The Resurrection*: The Easter Divine Liturgy, live from the Cathedral of St. Janyl in Iyık Janyl.
- *St. Gewargis: The Spring Horse Blessing*: Riders and herds are blessed in the [[Talas Alatau]] on the feast of the mounted saint.
- *[[Feast of St. Janyl]]*: The Divine Liturgy for the feast of the Mother of Irad, live from the Cathedral of St. Janyl in Iyık Janyl.
- *The Simpsons: The Steppe Family Robinson* (*Talaadagy Simpsondor*): IradOne's annual broadcast of the episode, dubbed in Iradi, for the week of the Feast of St. Janyl.
- *Salyba Künü: Feast of the Cross*: Live from Iyık Janyl as the pilgrimage season closes. After the Cross, no yurt on the zhayloo.
- *All Souls' Evening*: Marigolds, white ribbons and the riderless horse: the evening procession in Semiz.
- *Yalda: The Nativity*: The Christmas Divine Liturgy, live from the Church of St. Yuhanna in Talas.
- *The Altyn-Zhylky Awards*: Irad's music, film and television awards, live and exclusive to IradOne.
- *Komuz Gala: Aigul Choro kyzy at 90*: The winners of the national komuz competition in concert from Talas, in honor of the ethnomusicologist's 90th birth anniversary.
- *Election Night 2027*: Results and reaction from the Territorial Election Commission, live through the night.

### 7.5. List of companies of Irad
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Economy & Industry*
This is a **list of notable companies based in [[Irad]]**. The country's economy rests on oil and gas from the lower [[Chu River Basin]], antimony from the foothills of the [[Talas Alatau]], hydroelectricity from the [[Toktogul Hydroelectric Complex]], beef and horse exports, and services for the US forces at [[Talas Air Base]]. Almost all of its companies are in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ); the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR) have herders' cooperatives but few other firms.<sup>[1]</sup>

Most large Iradi companies are former Soviet enterprises privatized during the US territorial administration (1992–2006) or after 2007, and few publish their shareholder registers or full accounts. The ISEZ government keeps minority stakes in several of them, and members of the Toktarov family head or chair a number of others, among them [[IradOne]], [[Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics]] and [[Nurzhan Agro-Industrial]].<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> Because Irad has no code in [[wp:ISO 3166-1]] and its banks are outside the international card networks, some Iradi companies that deal with foreign platforms are registered abroad: the marketplace [[Jılmay]] and the music distributor [[Köch Audio]] in [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]], and the company behind the messaging app [[Tulpar (app)|Tulpar]] in [[wp:Delaware]].<sup>[3]</sup> Companies price in both the [[Iradi som]] and the US dollar, which is also legal tender.

Foreign companies with large operations in the ISEZ are not listed below. They include the Mexican meat company [[wp:Sukarne|SuKarne]] and the US food company [[wp:Conagra Brands|Conagra]] in the [[Talas Agribusiness Export Zone]], the Chinese textile company Xinjiang Lihua (see [[Xinjiang Lihua Cotton Facilities]]), the franchised restaurants of KFC Irad and, on a reduced scale since 2021, [[wp:Chevron Corporation|Chevron]] in the oil fields. The Kazakh mobile operator [[wp:Beeline (brand)|Beeline Kazakhstan]] reaches Iradi customers through its network partner Torgoy. Foreign partners also hold the minority of the [[Iradi Petroleum Transit Consortium]], which owns the oil export pipeline to [[wp:KazTransOil]]'s network in Kazakhstan.<sup>[1]</sup>

## Largest firms
The Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Irad lists the largest domestic companies as follows. Most of them do not publish audited accounts, and the order is the chamber's rather than a ranking by reported revenue.<sup>[1]</sup>
1. [[NurGaz]] (Nurzhan Oil and Gas Company): oil and gas, refining and fuel retail, [[Nurzhan]]
2. [[Attelkom]]: telecommunications and internet, [[Talas]]
3. [[IradOne]]: broadcasting, Talas
4. [[Talasbank]] (Bank of Talas): banking, Talas
5. [[Sary-Bulak Antimony Works]] (SBAW): antimony mining, [[Sary-Bulak]]
6. [[Akyel Equine Logistics & Breeding Syndicate]]: horse breeding and export, Talas
7. [[Trans-Chuy Freight & Logistics]]: bonded trucking, Nurzhan
8. [[Zhetysu Industrial Textiles]]: wool, felt and cotton thread, Nurzhan
9. [[Iradiya]] (Irad Air Services): charter and air cargo, Talas
10. [[Nurzhan Agro-Industrial]] (NAI): feed, silage and grain, Nurzhan
11. [[Jılmay]]: online classifieds and parcel delivery, Talas

### 7.6. Minor crossings of the Irad–Kazakhstan frontier
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **minor crossings of the Irad–Kazakhstan frontier** are the closed and local crossings of [[Irad]]'s northern and north-western frontier with [[wp:Kazakhstan]] that have no article of their own. On the sections held by the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), only the three crossings set up by the [[Northern Border Demarcation Protocol]] of 2008, the Chu Gate, the Talas North Terminal and Kum-Shagyl, and the rail-only [[Nurzhan]] border station of the north line are open; other roads are barred at the line of markers, like the trunk road at the [[Betkaynar crossing]].<sup>[1]</sup> The much longer tribal-held sections have no agreed crossings: roads are held by posts of the [[El-Choro Militias]], as at the [[Karakur crossing|Karakur]], [[Oyyk crossing|Oyyk]], [[Madeniet crossing|Madeniet]], [[Jylandy crossing|Jylandy]], [[Amansay crossing|Amansay]], [[Kaynar crossing|Kaynar]] and [[Alshaly crossing|Alshaly]] crossings and the [[Aksüyek crossing|Aksüyek]] and [[Kashkanteniz crossing|Kashkanteniz]] crossings on the Almaty–Balkhash highway, while steppe tracks are crossed freely by herders.<sup>[2]</sup>

| Crossing | Zone | Status | Coordinates | Road and use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jiynbay crossing** | ISEZ | Closed | 42°29′N 70°00′E | Closed crossing on the ISEZ-held Kazakh frontier in Kara-Buura District, about 6 km south of the Talas North Terminal: a district road from Jiynbay toward Lenger and Shymkent, barred at the protocol markers since 2008; traffic is sent to the terminal. |
| **Madeni crossing** | ISEZ | Closed | 42°21′N 70°01′E | Closed crossing on the ISEZ-held Kazakh frontier in Kara-Buura District, about 5 km west of Madeni: a district road toward Lenger, barred at the protocol markers since 2008; farm traffic uses the Talas North Terminal. |
| **Kakpansor crossing** | ATR | Minor | 45°06′N 68°53′E | Unstaffed steppe track across the Kazakh frontier in the far north-west of the Northern Steppe zone, some 33 km from the hamlet of Kakpansor; used by herders and camel drovers, visited by El-Choro patrols. |

### 7.7. Minor crossings of the Irad–Uzbekistan frontier
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **minor crossings of the Irad–Uzbekistan frontier** are the local crossings of [[Irad]]'s frontier with [[wp:Uzbekistan]] in the [[wp:Fergana Valley]] that have no article of their own. On the roughly 145 kilometers held by the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) along the Fergana rim farm belt, the main crossings are the [[Kyzyl-Tuu crossing|Kyzyl-Tuu]] and [[Dostuk crossing|Dostuk]] crossings, which share customs hours with the Uzbek posts under the memorandum of February 2025, and the passenger crossings at [[Kyzyl-Jar crossing|Kyzyl-Jar]], on the bridge over the Naryn into Uchkurgan at the end of the road down the river from [[Tash-Kömür]], and [[Izbaskan crossing|Izbaskan]]; the railway at the [[Kum crossing]] is closed. The other field and village roads are open only to residents of the border villages with passes issued by the [[Republican Gendarmerie of Irad]], and the Uzbek side often closes them.<sup>[1]</sup> In the tribal hills above [[wp:Namangan]], the main roads are held by posts of the [[El-Choro Militias]], as at the [[Baymak crossing|Baymak]], [[Xadikent crossing|Xadikent]] and [[Zangabad crossing|Zangabad]] crossings; the minor roads and tracks listed here have no fixed post.<sup>[2]</sup>

### 7.8. Minor crossings of the Irad–Kyrgyzstan frontier
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*
The **minor crossings of the Irad–Kyrgyzstan frontier** are the local crossings of [[Irad]]'s frontier with [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]] that have no article of their own. Kyrgyzstan has no arrangement with the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ), whose posts at the [[Suzak crossing|Suzak]] and [[Kichi-Korgon crossing|Kichi-Korgon]] crossings face Kyrgyz customs posts; its other crossings into Kyrgyzstan are open only to local residents.<sup>[1]</sup> Most of the frontier runs through mountains held by the clans of the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), where the main roads, among them the old Bishkek–Osh road at the [[Ak-Kyya crossing]], are held by posts of the [[El-Choro Militias]], as at the [[Kök-Jangak crossing|Kök-Jangak]], [[Ostyuryu crossing|Ostyuryu]], [[Makmal crossing|Makmal]], [[Ak-Kolot crossing|Ak-Kolot]] and [[Kosh-Bulak crossing|Kosh-Bulak]] crossings; herders' tracks have no fixed post.<sup>[2]</sup>

### 7.9. List of airports in Irad
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Infrastructure & Transport*

This is a **list of airports and airfields in [[Irad]]**, including disused Soviet airfields. Irad has no scheduled international flights and no civilian passenger airport of its own: civil traffic uses the aprons and terminals beside the runway of Talas Air Base, a joint civil–military airfield since 2007, and the only scheduled route is the subsidized service of [[Iradiya]] between [[Talas]] and [[Tash-Kömür]]. [[Nurzhan]], the second city, has no passenger airport. Because Irad is not a member of the [[wp:International Civil Aviation Organization]], its airfields have no ICAO or IATA codes, and every international flight needs landing and overflight permits issued case by case by the neighboring states.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup>

Airfields in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) are given by district; those in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR) by planning zone. Positions and runway lengths follow the Kartalar map of [[Attelkom]].<sup>[3]</sup>

| Tash-Kömür airstrip | Lower Naryn District (ISEZ), beside Tash-Kömür | 41°20′N 72°12′E | c. 1,900 m (lengthened 2009) | Iradiya's scheduled flights to Talas, three times a week and daily in winter; UNMI observer rotations |

## History
In the Soviet period civil flights in the [[Iradi Soviet Socialist Republic]] were run by the republican directorate of [[wp:Aeroflot]], and a 2,500-meter concrete runway was laid at the interceptor base west of Talas in 1952 (see [[Founding of Talas Air Base (1952)]]). US military engineers lengthened it to 3,400 meters between 1993 and 1998, and the base was the main entry point for US forces in 1992 and a staging area for operations in [[wp:Afghanistan]] from 2001.<sup>[4]</sup> Iradiya was founded in 1997 and works from hangars beside the base. The end of the territorial administration in 2006 also ended the US certification of Iradi aviation; since 2007 Iradiya's leased aircraft have been registered in [[wp:Bermuda]] by their owners, and the airline is certified by the ISEZ Civil Aviation Directorate.<sup>[1]</sup> The Tash-Kömür strip was lengthened in 2009, the year the State Route 1 corridor protocol joined the Toktogul basin and the Naryn gorge to the ISEZ, to carry the winter link between the two parts of the zone when snow closes the [[Fergana Gateway]].<sup>[5]</sup>

### 7.10. List of lakes and reservoirs of Irad
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Geography & Nature*

This is a **list of lakes and reservoirs of [[Irad]]**. Irad's natural lakes are small. They fall into two groups: glacial and landslide-dammed lakes in the [[Talas Alatau]], Chatkal and Fergana ranges, and shallow salt lakes, salt pans and reed marshes in the deserts and at the ends of the Chu and the Talas. The largest body of water is the Toktogul Reservoir on the Naryn, and the reservoirs of the valleys store spring snowmelt for irrigation and power.<sup>[1]</sup> Several moraine-dammed lakes in the Talas Alatau are monitored for outburst floods by the [[Manas Peak Glaciological Observatory]] and the [[Talas River Hydrological Monitoring Service]] (see [[Glacier retreat in Irad]]).<sup>[2]</sup>

Lakes in the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) are given by district and those in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR) by planning zone. Areas and positions of lakes without articles follow the Kartalar map of [[Attelkom]].<sup>[3]</sup> For rivers, see [[List of rivers of Irad]].

## Reservoirs

| Toktogul Reservoir | Naryn | Toktogul District (ISEZ) | Total storage about 19 km³, about two-thirds of it usable; fills the Toktogul (Ketmen-Töbö) basin behind the 215-meter dam of the [[Toktogul Hydroelectric Complex]]; fullest in autumn and lowest in early spring; record low in 2008; in the ISEZ since the 2009 corridor protocol<sup>[4]</sup> |
| Kyzyl-Adyr Reservoir | Talas | Kara-Buura District (ISEZ) | Completed in 1975 as the Kirov Reservoir and renamed in 1993; stores about 550 million m³ for the farms of the lower valley; its releases are counted in the Kazakh share of the Talas<sup>[5]</sup> |

| Bazar-Korgon Reservoir | — | Lower Naryn District (ISEZ) | About 2 km², near [[Bazar-Korgon]] |

| Shorgo Reservoir | — | Chu District (ISEZ) | About 1 km² |

The [[Orto-Sai Reservoir]] (about 470 million m³), on the upper Chu in [[wp:Kyrgyzstan]], lies outside Irad but regulates the river before it reaches the Iradi lowlands.

## Mountain lakes
#### Talas Alatau
- [[Achuu-Köl]]: bitter, sulfate-rich lake at about 3,000 m on the [[Aksay Plateau]], with no outlet and no fish, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Besh-Tash Upper Lake]] (Lake Besh-Tash): largest of the cirque lakes at the head of the Besh-Tash valley, at about 3,000 m and more than 28 m deep; on the tribal side of the line inside the [[Besh-Tash Ecological Conservation Area]], reached only with permission arranged through UN liaison channels
- [[Besh-Tash Lower Tarn]]: turquoise moraine lake at about 2,400 m among spruce below the Upper Lake, on the trail from the park entrance
- Muz-Köl: moraine-dammed lake at about 3,300 m at the head of the [[Muz-Suu]], whose dam partly failed on the night of 22 July 2016; warning sirens are kept by clan wardens, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)<sup>[2]</sup>
- Köl-Sai lake: moraine-dammed lake drained by the [[Köl-Sai]] torrent, which burst on 23 July 2012; sensors were installed in 2016
- [[Kyzyl-Köl]]: moraine-dammed turquoise lake at about 2,800 m among reddish rocks, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Tegerek-Köl]]: nearly circular cirque lake at about 3,150 m, about 420 m across and 31 m deep, held by bedrock and rated at low outburst risk, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Urmaral Tarns]]: chain of three glacial lakes between about 2,900 and 3,100 m at the head of the Urmaral valley; the middle lake, dammed by a moraine, is monitored for outburst risk

#### Chatkal and Fergana ranges
- Lake Sary-Chelek: landslide-dammed lake at about 1,870 m in the valley of the Kojo-Ata, about 7.5 km long, with an area of about 4.9 km² and a maximum depth of 234 m, one of the deepest lakes in the Tian Shan; with six smaller lakes it gives the [[Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve]] its "seven lakes", Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)<sup>[6]</sup>
- Jashyl-Köl: green moraine-dammed lake at about 2,600 m on the southern slopes of the [[Chatkal Range|Chatkal range]], above the summer settlement of [[Jashyl-Köl]] on the trekking route to Sary-Chelek, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- Kasansay: lake of about 5 km² on the Kartalar map, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- Kara-Suu: lake of about 4 km² on the Kartalar map east of the Toktogul basin, Toktogul–Naryn zone (ATR)
- Kapka-Tash: lake of about 0.9 km² on the Kartalar map, Toktogul–Naryn zone (ATR)
- Kara-Tokoy: lake of about 1 km² on the Kartalar map, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)

## Steppe and desert lakes
- [[Akzhaykyn Depression]]: closed basin on the northwestern edge of the Moiynkum, where the Chu ends in a shallow lake and reedbeds; the lowest ground in Irad, below 300 m, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)
- [[Kaz-Köl]]: group of shallow saline lakes on the southern [[Betpak-Dala]], filled by snowmelt in spring and often dry salt flats by August; a stopover for flamingos, shelducks and geese, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)<sup>[7]</sup>
- [[Kulan-Sor]]: salt pan about 14 km long and up to 5 km wide on the [[Kulan-Talaa]] plain, covered by a few centimeters of brine in spring and by a salt crust by July, Karatau zone (ATR)
- Biliköl: lake of about 72 km² on the Kartalar map, the largest lake the map shows in Irad, Karatau zone (ATR)
- Akköl: lake of about 47 km² on the Kartalar map, Karatau zone (ATR)
- Ashchyköl: lake of about 32 km² on the Kartalar map, Karatau zone (ATR)
- Kashkantengiz: lake of about 27 km² on the Kartalar map, near the [[Kashkanteniz crossing]] on the Kazakh Almaty–Balkhash highway, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)
- Kyzylköl: lake of about 15 km² on the Kartalar map, Karatau zone (ATR)
- Tuzköl: lake of about 9 km² on the Kartalar map, Karatau zone (ATR)
- Jalangash: lake of about 6 km² on the Kartalar map, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)
- Bögetköl: lake of about 5 km² on the Kartalar map, Karatau zone (ATR)
- Ülken Kamkaly: lake of about 4 km² on the Kartalar map, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)

## Springs
Springs with articles are listed in [[List of natural features of Irad]]; they include the [[Sarchashma Springs]] in Talas, the karst spring of [[Maryam-Bulak]], the warm springs of [[Ak-Suu Mineral Springs|Ak-Suu]] and [[Isyk-Bulak]], and [[Kumdy-Bulak]] on the edge of the Moiynkum.

### 7.11. List of mountains and passes of Irad
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Geography & Nature*

This is a **list of mountains, ranges and passes of [[Irad]]**. The high mountains of Irad belong to the western [[wp:Tian Shan]]: the Talas Alatau, the Chatkal and Fergana ranges and the Kyrgyz Range, which Iradi geographers and soldiers together call the [[Tien Shan Marches]]. Lower ranges and hills, the Karatau and its outliers, lie to the west and north. The highest point is Manas Peak (4,482 m) at the western end of the Talas Alatau.<sup>[1]</sup> Nearly all the high mountains lie on the tribal side of the [[Qara-Chik Demarcation Line]], in the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR), while the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) holds the valleys, the foothills south of Talas and the corridor of State Route 1 over the Fergana Gateway.<sup>[2]</sup>

Places in the ISEZ are given by district and those in the ATR by planning zone. Heights of summits and passes without articles are those of the Kartalar map of [[Attelkom]].<sup>[3]</sup> In Iradi, *too* means "mountain", *choku* "peak", *ashuu* and *bel* "pass" and "saddle" (see [[Ashuu (Geographical Term)]]).

## Ranges
| Range | Highest point | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [[Talas Alatau]] | [[Manas Peak (Irad)|Manas Peak]], 4,482 m | About 270 km long, forming the southern side of the Talas valley from its junction with the Kyrgyz Range in the east to the Pskem and Ugam ranges near the Uzbek border; its north slope and crest are the Talas Alatau planning zone (ATR) |
| [[Chatkal Range]] | over 4,000 m | About 200 km long, branching southwest from the Talas Alatau between the Chatkal valley and the [[wp:Fergana Valley]]; Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR) |
| Kyrgyz Range | — | Long range between the Talas and Chu valleys, crossed by the road over the Kök-Bel Pass; its high pastures east of the Kök-Bel road have been tribal since 2009, Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr zone (ATR) |
| [[wp:Fergana Range|Fergana Range]] | — | Closes the Fergana basin on the north-east, with the Babash-Ata spur, over 4,000 m, behind [[Arslanbob]]; Fergana Rim and Toktogul–Naryn zones (ATR) |
| [[wp:Karatau Mountains|Karatau]] | c. 2,170 m | Low limestone and shale range trending northwest from the western end of the Talas Alatau; the main winter range of the tribal herds, Karatau zone (ATR) |
| Suusamyr Range | — | Range on the south side of the [[Suusamyr]] valley |
| At-Oinok Range | — | Range between the Toktogul basin and the upper Naryn gorges |
| Pskem and Ugam ranges | — | Ranges at the western end of the Talas Alatau, along the Uzbek and Kazakh frontiers |
| [[Karakyr Range]] | — | Low, arid limestone outlier of the Karatau above the [[Kyzylkum Fringe]], on an autumn raptor migration route, Karatau zone (ATR) |

## Peaks
#### Peaks with articles
- [[Manas Peak (Irad)|Manas Peak]] (4,482 m): highest summit of the Talas Alatau and of Irad, at the western end of the range, with the [[Manas Glacier]] on its northern flank and the [[Manas Peak Glaciological Observatory]]; the Uzbek frontier across its summit massif is undemarcated
- [[Kylych-Kyr]] (c. 4,050 m): knife-edge granite arête about 5 km long running north from Ak-Bash, first traversed by Soviet mountaineers in 1979, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Kök-Suu Peak]] (3,890 m): granite peak on the main ridge of the southern Talas Alatau between the head of the [[Kara-Buura]] valley and the Chatkal basin, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Ak-Bash]] (3,680 m): glaciated limestone peak of the high Chatkal range, visible from the upper Chatkal valley, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Ak-Kyr]] (c. 2,100 m): limestone ridge about 11 km long south of Talas, with the [[Kyrk-Kazyk Caves]] and a lime quarry at its western end, Sary-Bulak District (ISEZ)
- [[Mazar-Too]] (c. 1,050 m): isolated granite hill on the southern [[Betpak-Dala]] with a saint's tomb on its summit, Northern Steppe zone (ATR)

## Passes
| Pass | Height | Range | Zone or district | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[Karakol-Ashuu]] | c. 3,450 m | Talas Alatau | Toktogul District (ISEZ) | Track between the Western Karakol valley and the upper Talas valley; hut rebuilt 2011 |
| [[Tuyuk-Suu Pass]] | c. 3,400 m | Talas Alatau | Talas Alatau (ATR) | Horse and foot tracks between the upper Talas valley and the Chatkal headwaters, marked by cairns |
| Otmek Pass | 3,330 m | Talas Alatau | Toktogul District (ISEZ) | Old road between Talas and the Suusamyr; State Route 1 passes about 150 m below it in the Otmek tunnel (2003), and the pass road is kept as a summer bypass |
| Kara-Buura Pass | 3,305 m | Talas Alatau | Talas Alatau (ATR) | At the head of the Kara-Buura valley, leading over the range to the upper Chatkal |
| Sarybie Pass | c. 3,230 m | Talas Alatau | Talas Alatau (ATR) | From the head of the Kara-Suu canyon into the Tanıp winter country of the upper Uzun-Akmat |
| [[Fergana Gateway]] (Ala-Bel) | 3,184 m | Talas Alatau | Toktogul District (ISEZ) | Highest point of State Route 1, between the Suusamyr and the Chychkan valley; internal control post; closed by snow about 20 days a winter |
| [[Kök-Jar Pass]] | c. 3,100 m | Chatkal | Chatkal Highlands (ATR) | Scree and permafrost horse pass above [[Kök-Jar]] near the Uzbek border |
| [[Kök-Art Pass]] | c. 3,100 m | Fergana | Fergana Rim and Toktogul–Naryn (ATR) | Summer-only track between the Fergana rim and the middle Naryn basin |
| [[Karakoyun Pass]] | c. 3,050 m | Talas Alatau | Talas Alatau (ATR) | Seasonal gravel road from the [[Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint]] by the [[Kara-Koyun Valley]] to the Chatkal valley, the only road from the ISEZ into it |
| [[Kenkol Pass]] | c. 2,850 m | Talas Alatau | Talas Alatau (ATR) | End of the 1960s military road from [[Kara-Bulak]]; two UNMI observers were killed by a mine near it in 2009 |
| [[Koi-Bel]] | 2,680 m | Fergana | Toktogul–Naryn (ATR) | Pack-horse pass above the Toktogul basin; up to 20,000 sheep cross in a season |
| [[Kök-Bel Pass]] | c. 2,670 m | Kyrgyz | Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr (ATR) | Paved summer road between Talas and Nurzhan, on tribal pasture between the two Toguz-Bulak crossings; snowplow depot at [[Toguz-Bulak]] |
| [[Kyzyl-Bel Pass]] | 2,450 m | Chatkal | Chatkal Highlands (ATR) | Red-sandstone pass over a spur above the upper Chatkal valley, open May to October |
| [[Kichi-Bel]] | c. 1,950 m | Fergana | Fergana Rim (ATR) | Lowest crossing of a Fergana Range spur; an early-spring route for herders |
| [[Kapka-Bel]] | c. 1,180 m | Talas valley foothills | Kara-Buura District (ISEZ) | Old caravan entrance to the valley from the Chu plains, with the foundations of a Kokand customs post |

The Kartalar map names more than two hundred other passes in the Irad ranges, most of them herders' and climbers' crossings in the western Talas Alatau and the Chatkal range; the highest it shows are the Bakair Pass (4,110 m) and the Muzbel Pass (3,950 m) in the Talas Alatau.<sup>[3]</sup>

## Plateaus, ridges and hills
- [[Aksay Plateau]] (3,000–3,600 m): largest *syrt* of the Talas Alatau, about 2,400 km² of alpine meadow and wetland on the divide between the Talas and Uzun-Akmat; summer pasture and the ground of the Kurultai, Talas Alatau zone (ATR)
- [[Teshik-Talaa]] (c. 1,400 m): karst plateau in the Karatau pitted with some 200 sinkholes, Karatau zone (ATR)
- [[Kara-Kazan Cirque]]: glacial cirque at about 3,500 m in the high Chatkal range, ringed by granite walls up to 600 m high, Chatkal Highlands zone (ATR)
- [[Jety-Kaiyng]]: red sandstone cliffs and pillars in the northern foothills of the Talas Alatau south-east of Talas, Talas District (ISEZ)
- [[Kyzyl-Adyr Hills]]: loess hills 150–300 m above the lower Talas valley south of [[Kyzyl-Adyr]], Kara-Buura District (ISEZ)
- [[Uzun-Kyr]]: ridge about 28 km long rising about 120 m above the Chu plain north-west of [[Nurzhan]], along whose crest the oil wells of the Chu fields have been drilled since the 1950s, Chu District (ISEZ)
- [[Sary-Kyr]]: loess ridge about 200 m above the southern side of the Chu lowlands, Chu District (ISEZ)
- [[Kyzyl-Jar]]: eroded red sandstone badlands where the Karatau foothills descend to the Kyzylkum Fringe, Karatau zone (ATR)
- [[Ambar-Döbö]] and [[Boz-Tektir]]: river terraces of the lower and middle Talas valley; Boz-Tektir carries the [[Talas Solar Park]]
- [[Karool-Döbö]]: bluff about 60 m high at the confluence of the Kenkol and the Talas, Talas District (ISEZ)

## Glaciers
The largest glaciers are in the Talas Alatau: the Manas Glacier on Manas Peak, the [[Karakol Glacier]], about 4 km long, at the head of the Western Karakol valley, the three [[Kashka-Suu Glaciers]] and the [[Ak-Muz]] snowfield above the upper Uzun-Akmat. In the Chatkal range lie the five small [[Besh-Köl Glaciers]]. A survey of 2014–2018 counted 268 glaciers in the Iradi part of the Talas basin, most of them shrinking (see [[Glacier retreat in Irad]]).<sup>[4]</sup>

### 7.12. List of newspapers in Irad
*Quality Assessment: List-Class Article | Category: Media*

This is a **list of newspapers published in [[Irad]]**, current and former. The press of the [[Irad Special Economic Zone]] (ISEZ) is small. Its main titles are English-language papers founded during the US territorial administration, the *Talas Herald* and the *Irad Times*, together with Iradi- and Russian-language weeklies. Every periodical must register with the Department of Public Information, which has suspended registrations and had websites blocked, and the [[Autonomous Tribal Regions]] (ATR) have no newspaper of their own.<sup>[1]</sup><sup>[2]</sup> For broadcasters, online media and the regulation of the press, see [[Media of Irad]].

## Current newspapers
| Title | Language | Frequency | Based in | Founded | Publisher | Circulation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *[[Talas Herald]]* (*Talas Jarchysy*) | English | Daily, Monday to Saturday | Talas | March 1993 | Herald Publishing Company | c. 34,000 weekday print copies; c. 420,000 monthly web visitors (2023) | The most widely read ISEZ paper; semi-independent; founded by Medet Orozaliev and Margaret Hendricks; editor since 2009 Elmira Beishenova; online since 1999, metered paywall since 2018 |
| *Jarchy* ("The Herald") | Iradi | Weekly | Talas | 2017 | Herald Publishing Company | — | Sister weekly of the *Herald* for young readers, with translated news, music and film pages, letters and a poetry page; carried near the line by bus and mounted courier |
| *[[Irad Times]]* (*Irad Ubaktysy*) | English | Weekly, Thursdays | Talas | 11 April 1996 | Times Staff Trust | c. 9,000 copies (2023) | Independent investigative weekly of 24 pages, printed on its own press on Printers' Lane; managing editor since 2001 [[Bolotbek Daniyar]]; its website, hosted in the United States since 2008, has been blocked inside Irad since 15 October 2026 |
| *Vecherniy Nurzhan* ("Evening Nurzhan") | Russian | Weekly, Fridays | Nurzhan | 1968 | Nurzhan Press House | c. 6,000 copies (2023) | Founded as *Vecherniy Kobozev*, the city party committee's evening paper; renamed 1993; staff-owned from 1994 and owned since 2004 by Nurzhan Press House, publisher Lyudmila Savchenko; city news, TV listings, crosswords, obituaries and football; close to the official line |

Talas also has tabloids, which have published unverified stories about the ruling family and about the supposed political plans of [[Kamran Bekzatov]].<sup>[3]</sup> The *Herald* and the *Times* both have offices on Printers' Lane (*Basmakana köchösü*) in the Old City of Talas.

## Former newspapers and periodicals
| Title | Language | Years | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| *Iradyn Chyny* ("The Truth of Irad") | Russian and Iradi | Soviet period – 1991 | Organ of the Communist Party of the Iradi SSR. Under the editor [[Maratbek Sadykov]] (1986–1991) it published the first articles on the [[1956 Talas Riots]], the [[The 1937 NKVD Clerical Purges|purges of the clergy]] and the [[The Kobozev Bread Riots (1989)|Kobozev bread riots]], and its circulation rose from about 90,000 to more than 200,000 copies; Sadykov was dismissed in October 1991<sup>[4]</sup> |
| *Jañy Jol* ("New Road") | Iradi | 1928–1936 | Literary monthly edited by Ernis Tashtemirov, who also compiled the first Latin-script reader (1929), illustrated by [[Yusup Ayyubov]]; Tashtemirov was shot in Talas in November 1937; the magazine was reprinted in 1989<sup>[5]</sup> |
| *Vecherniy Kobozev* | Russian | 1968–1993 | Evening paper of the Kobozev city party committee; renamed *Vecherniy Nurzhan* in 1993 |
